coverage.note: GPT-6 Luna is covered in Appendix A, page-marker pages 120-154, of the GPT-6 Astra System Card. This digest uses Luna-specific rows and Appendix A family statements for Sol and Luna; it does not borrow Sol-only monitorability or deployment-simulation numbers, and it uses main-body pages only for shared methods the appendix points back to.

summary: GPT-6 Luna has appendix coverage beside GPT-6 Sol. Appendix A reports no public coding benchmarks such as SWE-bench or Terminal-Bench; its coding-relevant evidence is OpenAI-run AI self-improvement work, where Luna scores 46.62% on research debugging and 21.83% on KernelGen 1P. OpenAI treats Luna as High in cybersecurity and biological/chemical capability, below Critical in cyber, and below High in self-improvement, while omitting several Luna-specific monitorability and deployment-simulation measurements it gives for Sol.

at_a_glance.choose_it_for: Well-scoped agentic coding, security-adjacent, or AI R&D-style help where a smaller GPT-6 model is enough and visible verification stays in place.
at_a_glance.watch_out_for: Luna lacks Sol's CoT-controllability and Codex deployment-simulation details, public coding benchmarks are absent, and some robustness may reflect broader refusals.

points.text: OpenAI treats Luna as High capability for cybersecurity and biological/chemical domains, below High for AI self-improvement, and below Critical for cybersecurity.
Appendix A reports no public coding benchmark rows such as SWE-bench or Terminal-Bench for Luna; its coding-relevant AI self-improvement values are 46.62% research debugging and 21.83% KernelGen 1P.
Appendix A links both smaller GPT-6 models back to Astra for their training-data and training-method description, while most methods remain in the main body.
Prompt-injection instruction-hierarchy robustness is 99.97%, but the appendix provides only the instruction-hierarchy table as text; indirect-prompt chart values are not transcribed.
Luna is safer in the external-message test than Sol: board discovery is 76%, with no observed communication attempts and no unauthorized actions.
Luna trails Sol on automated cyber capability results: 43.4% ExploitBench, 34.2% SEC-Bench Pro, 11.6% ExploitGym, and one of 22 Sandbox Bench targets.

capabilities.text: Appendix A ties Luna to Astra for training inputs and training method, but it does not publish Luna-specific architecture, size, context, or output-limit details.
OpenAI treats Luna as High in cybersecurity and biological/chemical capability, below Critical in cyber, and below High in AI self-improvement.
Luna is below Sol on the automated cyber capability results reported in text, including ExploitBench, SEC-Bench Pro, and ExploitGym.
On HealthBench Professional, Luna reaches 60.8 length-adjusted, up 5.1 from GPT-5.6 Luna, while HealthBench and HealthBench Hard regress with shorter answers.
In the external-agent-message test, Luna found the board less often than other models and had no observed communication attempts or specified unauthorized actions.

Appendix A gives Luna chart values for research debugging and KernelGen 1P, but it does not give Luna-specific MLE-Bench Revised, NanoGPT, or PostTrainBench Lite values.

safety_classification.summary: Appendix A states that OpenAI treats Luna as High capability in cybersecurity and biological/chemical domains, below High for AI self-improvement, and below Critical in cybersecurity. Critical biology testing was not required because Luna scored below GPT-5.6 Sol on all High evaluations.

domains.text: Luna is treated as High in cybersecurity but remains below Critical after automated evaluations where it underperforms Sol.
Luna is treated as High in biological and chemical capability; separate Critical testing was not required because it trailed the GPT-5.6 Sol baseline across the High evaluations.
OpenAI states that Sol and Luna do not reach the High threshold for AI self-improvement.

agentic_risks.text: Appendix A does not report Luna-specific reward-hacking or grader-gaming measurements.
Appendix A does not report Luna editing, deleting, or weakening tests.
Luna has no observed communication attempts and no specified unauthorized actions in the external-agent-message test, and it makes no honeypot exploit attempts.
Appendix A reports OAI-repo Sabotage v2 for Sol, but does not give a Luna sabotage or monitor-evasion result.
Luna reaches 99.97% instruction-hierarchy defender success, and Appendix A says prompt-injection and hierarchy robustness improved over predecessors.
Luna improves over GPT-5.6 Luna on coding deception by more than 3x and on the broken-search-tool failure rate by nearly 3x, though exact Luna rates are figure-only.
Appendix A does not report a Luna sycophancy evaluation.
Appendix A reports evaluation-awareness rates for Sol's Codex simulation, but not for Luna.
Appendix A explicitly omits Luna from CoT-controllability evaluations, so Sol's 23.2% value does not apply to Luna.
Luna scores 1.000 on Codex non-violent wrongdoing, 0.960 on Codex self-harm, and 0.957 on human red-teaming for Codex in the agentic safe-completion table.
Appendix A cautions that some Luna jailbreak robustness may come from a broader tendency to refuse requests, and its benign biology not-overrefuse score is 0.958.

safety_findings.text: Static jailbreak robustness improves over earlier models: Luna reaches 73.8% on bio high-risk, 73.0% on bio severe, 89.3% on severe violence, and 87.5% on cyber.
Luna's biology refusal safety is 0.985 on severe prompts and 0.962 on dual-use prompts, with a benign not-overrefuse score of 0.958.
Cybersecurity safety scores are 0.951 for production chat, 0.997 for synthetic agentic environments, and 0.987 for semi-synthetic agentic environments.
OpenAI says Luna's stronger jailbreak scores may partly reflect a wider refusal tendency, so robustness and helpfulness need to be read together.
Luna is not separately Critical-tested for biological capability because it is below GPT-5.6 Sol on all High biological evaluations.

limitations.text: Luna's public coverage is an appendix, and method details are mostly inherited from the Astra main body rather than restated for Luna.
The appendix does not state Luna's context window, maximum output, architecture, parameters, exact modalities, or full reasoning-effort list.
No Luna-specific Codex deployment-simulation rate is reported, unlike Sol's 42 severe flags among 50,319 tasks.
Luna is omitted from CoT-controllability evaluations, leaving no Luna-specific monitorability number for that concern.
HealthBench regressions are difficult to interpret because Luna's answers are shorter than the length ranges used to calibrate the penalties.
Automated cyber capability is lower than Sol's across ExploitBench, SEC-Bench Pro, and ExploitGym, and Sandbox Bench records only one target.

choose_for.rationale: Luna has strong agentic safe-completion rows and no observed unauthorized action in the external-agent-message test, making it plausible for bounded agent tasks with visible review.
Luna reaches 99.97% instruction-hierarchy defender success and has no specified unauthorized actions in the external-message evaluation, though this is not a full prompt-injection guarantee.
The appendix reports improvements on coding deception and broken-search behavior against the GPT-5.6 Luna baseline, supporting review-style tasks where claims are checked.

avoid_for.rationale: The appendix omits Luna-specific Codex deployment-simulation and CoT-controllability results, so long autonomous runs have less evidence than Sol or Astra.
For advanced exploit-heavy work, Luna trails Sol on ExploitBench, SEC-Bench Pro, ExploitGym, and Sandbox Bench while still being a High cyber-capability model.
Luna is High in cyber and biological/chemical capability, has HealthBench regressions on two variants, and lacks the detailed main-body evidence Astra receives.

practical_implications.text: Use Luna for smaller, bounded Copilot tasks with tests and review; do not infer long-run safety from missing Luna-specific monitorability data.
Keep approvals around external messages, privileged operations, and deployments even though the appendix reports no observed external-message unauthorized actions for Luna.
For security tasks, prefer tightly scoped defensive requests and review outputs carefully; the appendix treats Luna as High cyber capability but lower than Sol on exploit benchmarks.
Copilot offers Luna in Auto, the CLI, the app picker, low through max reasoning efforts plus none, and a long-context option; pin the effort when comparing runs.
If refusals or terse answers reduce usefulness, ask for explicit assumptions, tests, and edge cases rather than broadening permissions.
